pride_data.title: Cross-linking mass spectrometry analysis of human BCL7A and BAF47 in presence and absence of nucleosome
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the interaction between BCL7A and BAF47 and their respective interactions with nucleosomes. The two proteins were cross-linked with two different concentrations of disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS) in presence and absence of nucleosomes.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Cross-linking was performed according to previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014) with two DSS concentrations, 0.25 and 1 mM. Cross-linked proteins were digested in solution using endoproteinase Lys-C and trypsin and fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography. LC-MS/MS analysis was performed on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer.  Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest/xProphet (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.5, against the sequences of the target proteins (including canonical H2, H3 and H4 histone sequences) and identified contaminants/copurified proteins (human keratins, proteins from the E. coli expression system). Important xQuest search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm. Reactive sites for DSS were K and the protein N terminus.  The false discovery rate was controlled by searching against reversed sequences. Due to the small number of target identifications, an accurate estimation of false discovery rates is difficult. However, over all data sets only two decoy hits remained in the curated identification lists. The table “File_list.xlsx” allows the assignment of different sample types, SEC fractions and replicates to the corresponding .raw files. Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
